multiplier_evidence: Measured 2026-08-23/24 from finished ConGen folds against condition-A references (mean total_ms/3.6e6 per fold, data/results_conmin/*_long.csv, condition A, which carries negatives = n/a and so does no NE encoding at all -- the reference is not a raw/reduced mixture). ConGen ran at 0.10x-0.50x of condition A on every cell with a reference, so the handoff's premise that these estimates are FLOORS is falsified: they are ceilings by 2x-10x. DERIVATION of congen_multiplier: the worst observed PER-FOLD ratio across all of that KB's cells, including cells whose reference is under 0.01 h and whose ratio is dominated by interpreter start-up, rounded up to the next conservative step. It is deliberately looser than the per-cell figures in congen_multiplier_observed -- rounding up can only make the queue decline a unit it could have run, never start one it cannot finish. CAUSE: located in per-check cost, not in the amount of work (check counts agree at 0.98-1.09 with condition A). NE form is eliminated -- raw vs reduced moves wall-clock by -2.06% to +1.69% with identical check counts -- and NE presence points the wrong way, since extra clauses would make ConGen slower, not 8x faster. Remaining candidate is checker-level, by elimination rather than evidence; fqa is unexplained. See plans/reports/measurement-260823-2347-congen-condition-a-ratio-mechanism-report.md. NOT PROJECTABLE: the ratio has no size law in the measured range, so it cannot be extrapolated to busybox. busybox charges the full condition-A estimate via 'default' until it has a measurement of its own.
